topic: Neural Network Learning: The Intuitive Backpropagation
target_audience: University students (STEM majors) or tech-curious beginners

sections.title: The Analogy: The Guessing Game
lecture_lines: Neural networks start as simple guessing machines.
They classify inputs into random, wrong categories.
A robot guesses cat versus dog pixels.
animations: Show a simple neural network schematic with nodes initialized to random state. Color nodes #FFFFFF. Place using grid constraints [B004].
Show random, incorrect output classifications (e.g., 'Cat' and 'Dog' labels) flashing in red (#FF0000). Place using [B019].
Represent the input as a pixel grid (2x2) and highlight guesses fluctuating randomly. Place using [B004].

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Error Surface
lecture_lines: We visualize error as a mountainous landscape.
Low valleys represent the ideal minimum error.
A ball rolls downhill, seeking the lowest point.
animations: Display a 3D-like mountain landscape (loss surface) in shades of blue (#87CEEB). Place in Rows A-C per [B019].
Highlight the deep center of the mountain landscape in #00FF00 (green) per [B022]. Place in Rows D-F per [B019].
Show a small ball in #FF4500 (orange) rolling from a high peak down toward the green valley, avoiding gutter at Column 3 [B004].

sections.title: The Core Concept: Backpropagation (The Blame Game)
lecture_lines: Backpropagation is the game of assigning blame.
We trace error backward, layer by layer.
Each neuron receives feedback on its contribution.
animations: Show a multi-layer network with nodes using. Text 'Error' appears at the output layer. Use [B019] for layer assignment.
Use green (#00FF00) directional arrows per [B035] to animate signal traveling backward through connections.
Highlight individual in yellow (#FFFF00) as they receive feedback signal and 'blame' value, adhering to [B004] gutter rules.

sections.title: The Math: Chain Rule in Motion
lecture_lines: The chain rule connects small weight changes.
It acts as a precise mathematical multiplier.
Tiny changes ripple through connected network gears.
animations: Show a series of gears linked together representing weight connections. Color gears #A9A9A9. Use [B037] and [B019] for layout.
Animate gear rotation sequentially using small white (#FFFFFF) tick marks to indicate mathematical multiplication. Use [B035] arrows.
Show ripples of light in cyan (#00FFFF) passing through the gear train when one is rotated, respecting [B004].

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
lecture_lines: Forward pass guesses, calculating initial error.
Backward pass adjusts weights, reducing error.
Repetition makes the network progressively smarter.
animations: Display two panels: 'Forward' (Rows A-C) and 'Backward' (Rows D-F) per [B019]. Use white color #FFFFFF.
Animate a loop where 'Forward' results in an 'Error' value, then 'Backward' modifies a weight represented by. Adhere to [B004].
Show a counter of 'Epochs' increasing, with the 'Error' value progressively decreasing and changing color to bright green (#00FF00). Use [B035] style for indicators.
